segments.t: Barinov is alone with Alisa, and the restaurant can wait. His daughter, who is about to say a lot about her parents, asks him a simple question. You'll hear it all in Russian before I explain a thing.
Алиса, как тебе мой ресторан?
Пап, смотри, я похожа на тебя?
Конечно, солнышко!
У тебя мои глаза и улыбка.
А мама говорит другое.
Она говорит, слава богу, не похожа!
Это она так шутит.
Не обращай внимания.
А ты тоже красивый, пап?
Я самый красивый повар в Москве!
Но мама говорит, ты очень смешной.
Мама просто завидует моему таланту.
Тогда давай играть дальше!
Я всегда готов играть с тобой.
Now we'll go over it.
Алиса, как тебе мой ресторан?
'Alisa, how do you like my restaurant?' The Russian is "how to you my restaurant?", with no verb at all. "Moy" is "my". Barinov shows off the place to his daughter like a man opening his own palace.
Пап, смотри, я похожа на тебя?
'Dad, look, do I look like you?' "Pap" is short for "papa", and "smotri" is "look". Then it's "similar to you". The -a on the end of the Russian for "similar" tells you the speaker is a girl.
Конечно, солнышко!

'Of course, sunshine!' "Solnyshko" is "little sun", a pet name people use for a child. And "konechno", "of course", is spelled with a ch but said with a sh. That's one of the first oddities you hear in Russian.
У тебя мои глаза и улыбка.
'You have my eyes and smile.' It's the "at you" pattern once more: "at you my eyes and smile". "Glaza" is "eyes", and "ulybka" is "smile". Barinov is warm about it, and a little too quick.
А мама говорит другое.

'And mom says something else.' The little word "a" means "and" or "but", and here it turns the corner. "Drugoe" is "other", so "says other" means "says something different". Alisa repeats it exactly as she heard it.
Она говорит, слава богу, не похожа!

'She says, thank God, you do not look like him!' "Slava bogu" is "glory to God", the everyday Russian "thank God". There's no "you" in the second half, just "ne pokhozha", "not similar". Alisa passes on her mother's joke word for word.
Это она так шутит.
'She was just joking.' The Russian is in the present: "it she so jokes". "Tak" means "like this" or "that way". Barinov is quick to wave it away, with a straight face.
Не обращай внимания.
'Do not pay any attention.' It's a fixed phrase, literally "don't turn attention". "Vnimanie", "attention", is the word printed on Russian warning signs, the way English signs say "Caution!".
А ты тоже красивый, пап?
'Are you handsome too, Dad?' "Krasivy" means beautiful, and Russians use it for handsome men too. "Tozhe" is "also". It's the question a child asks, and the one a father can't resist answering.
Я самый красивый повар в Москве!
'I am the most handsome chef in Moscow!' "Samy" is "the most", and it sits right before the describing word. "Moskva" becomes "Moskve" after "v", "in", when it means where something is.
Но мама говорит, ты очень смешной.
'But mom says you are very funny.' "Smeshnoy" means funny, and it can also mean laughable. Alisa doesn't know which her mother means. "Ochen", "very", sits in front of it, exactly as in English.
Мама просто завидует моему таланту.
'Mom is simply jealous of my talent.' "Zaviduet" is "envies", and Russian envies "to" something, so it's "envies to my talent", "moemu talantu". "Prosto" is "simply". It's a very Barinov explanation.
Тогда давай играть дальше!

'Then let us keep playing!' "Togda" is "then". "Davay" literally means "give", but in front of another verb it's "let's". "Dalshe" is "further". She changes the subject like a child who's had enough of grown-up talk.
Я всегда готов играть с тобой.

'I am always ready to play with you.' "Gotov" is "ready" and "vsegda" is "always". That's the soft side of the chef, said plainly. This is the line that makes you like him. Listen again, and see how much more you catch.
Алиса, как тебе мой ресторан?
Пап, смотри, я похожа на тебя?
Конечно, солнышко!
У тебя мои глаза и улыбка.
А мама говорит другое.
Она говорит, слава богу, не похожа!
Это она так шутит.
Не обращай внимания.
А ты тоже красивый, пап?
Я самый красивый повар в Москве!
Но мама говорит, ты очень смешной.
Мама просто завидует моему таланту.
Тогда давай играть дальше!
Я всегда готов играть с тобой.
Under the joking, Barinov is clearly happy to have Alisa with him. They keep playing. Goodbye for now.
Пока!
